stories.notes: Story has empty acceptance criteria and describes a complex cross-platform (GO, UP, MX) live preview feature in a CMS. Needs openspec to elaborate requirements and define AC with technical depth, then speckit to harden with testability, security, and edge-case coverage. High complexity and high risk warrant both agents in sequence.

agentContributions.notes: Novel story — live preview capability does not exist in the codebase. useContent is the central integration point (236+ consumers). Contentstack is unreachable at test time, so VCs assume a mocked preview API. VCs derived entirely from description since ACs are empty.

Openspec provided empty ACs, so all criteria are new. Derived from: (1) story title '[GO, UP, MX] Live Preview of Content in CMS' implying real-time draft preview across GO, UP, MX markets; (2) openspec's note that useContent is the central integration point with 236+ consumers — AC-14 ensures backward compatibility when preview is off; (3) openspec's note that Contentstack is unreachable at test time — ACs are written as observable outcomes testable with a controlled preview API. CAVEAT: Without access to the actual useContent hook, existing CMS integration code, or Contentstack preview SDK documentation, these ACs are derived from general live-preview patterns and may need refinement once implementation context is available. AC-10 (sanitization) and AC-11 (auth gating) address security. AC-13 addresses accessibility. AC-4/5/6/8/9 address edge cases and error handling. AC-15 covers referenced content resolution. AC-16 covers multi-consumer consistency. AC-17 covers localization, implied by the multi-market [GO, UP, MX] scope.

coordinatorReview.reviewNotes: Both agents added meaningful, non-overlapping value in their analysis: openspec identified useContent as the central integration point (236+ consumers) and the test-time constraint that Contentstack is unreachable, while speckit derived 17 detailed acceptance criteria covering testability, security (AC-10 sanitization, AC-11 auth gating), edge cases (AC-4/5/6/8/9), accessibility (AC-13), localization (AC-17), and backward compatibility (AC-14). However, there is a critical contradiction: the acceptanceCriteria array is empty, both agents report acceptanceChanged: false, and splitCount is 0 — yet speckit's notes explicitly state 'all criteria are new' and enumerate AC-1 through AC-17. The spec work was described in agent notes but never materialized into the story's acceptanceCriteria array. The collaborative analysis is sound and the proposed ACs appear complete, testable, and non-overlapping, but the deliverable is incomplete. A human must either manually apply the 17 ACs from speckit's notes into the acceptanceCriteria array or re-run the pipeline to ensure deltas are applied. No story split was performed, which is acceptable given this is a single cohesive feature, though the complexity (cross-platform GO/UP/MX, 236+ consumers) may warrant splitting during implementation planning.
